title: A Machine-Oriented Logic Based on the Resolution Principle
abstract_short: Introduces the resolution principle for automated theorem proving, combining substitution and truth-functional analysis into a single inference rule with unification.

title: Predicate Logic as Programming Language
abstract_short: Shows that predicate logic can serve as a practical programming language, interpreting implications as procedure declarations. Foundation of logic programming and Prolog.

title: The Semantics of Predicate Logic as a Programming Language
abstract_short: Defines operational and fixpoint semantics of predicate logic programs, establishes the least Herbrand model and T_P operator as foundations for logic programming semantics.

title: Negation as Failure
abstract_short: Introduces the completed database semantics and shows that the negation-as-failure inference rule only derives negated facts inferable from the completed database axioms.

title: Rete: A Fast Algorithm for the Many Pattern/Many Object Pattern Match Problem
abstract_short: Describes the Rete algorithm for efficient pattern matching in production systems, using a network of nodes to share comparisons across rules.

title: The Complexity of Relational Query Languages
abstract_short: Studies data and expression complexity of logical and algebraic query languages, establishing fundamental complexity bounds for relational calculus, fixpoint logic, and transitive closure extensions.

title: Foundations of Logic Programming
abstract_short: Comprehensive textbook establishing the theoretical foundations of logic programming including model theory, fixpoint theory, SLD-resolution, and negation.

title: An Amateur's Introduction to Recursive Query Processing Strategies
abstract_short: Surveys and compares strategies for processing recursive queries in relational databases, including naive, semi-naive, magic sets, counting, and other evaluation methods.

title: Magic Sets and Other Strange Ways to Implement Logic Programs
abstract_short: Introduces the magic set transformation for optimizing bottom-up evaluation of Datalog programs, along with counting and reverse counting methods for linear recursion.

title: Towards a Theory of Declarative Knowledge
venue: Foundations of Deductive Databases and Logic Programming
abstract_short: Introduces stratified logic programs, forbidding recursion through negation, and provides a declarative semantics based on iterated fixpoints for handling negation in Datalog.

title: The Stable Model Semantics for Logic Programming
abstract_short: Introduces stable model semantics for logic programs with negation, providing a non-monotonic reasoning framework that became the foundation of Answer Set Programming.

title: Principles of Database and Knowledge-Base Systems
abstract_short: Comprehensive two-volume textbook covering database theory including relational query languages, Datalog, logic as a data model, query optimization, and deductive databases.

title: What You Always Wanted to Know About Datalog (And Never Dared to Ask)
abstract_short: Tutorial presenting Datalog syntax, semantics, safety, and optimization methods including magic sets and counting, establishing Datalog as a practical query language.

title: Bottom-Up Beats Top-Down for Datalog
abstract_short: Proves that for any safe Datalog program, semi-naive bottom-up evaluation is at least as efficient as top-down evaluation, settling the evaluation strategy debate.

title: The Well-Founded Semantics for General Logic Programs
abstract_short: Introduces the well-founded semantics for logic programs with negation, providing a three-valued semantics that is always defined, unique, and computable in polynomial time.

title: Datalog Extensions for Database Queries and Updates
venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
abstract_short: Presents deterministic and non-deterministic extensions of Datalog with fixpoint semantics, characterizing their expressive power relative to complexity classes PTIME and PSPACE.

title: The Birth of Prolog
abstract_short: Historical account of Prolog's creation in 1972, born from natural language processing research at Marseille, describing the evolution from Q-systems to the definitive Prolog language.

title: Modular Stratification and Magic Sets for Datalog Programs with Negation
abstract_short: Defines modular stratification for Datalog with negation and extends magic set optimization to handle stratified negation, ensuring termination and correctness.

title: Foundations of Databases: The Logical Level
abstract_short: Definitive textbook on database theory covering relational calculus, Datalog, complexity of query evaluation, fixpoint logics, and the expressiveness hierarchy of query languages.

title: Finding Regular Simple Paths in Graph Databases
abstract_short: Studies regular path queries in graph databases: finding node pairs connected by paths whose label sequences match a regular expression. Shows intractability in general but polynomial cases.

title: Program Analysis via Graph Reachability
abstract_short: Formulates program analysis problems as CFL-reachability problems on graphs, establishing the connection between context-free language reachability and Datalog chain programs.

title: Descriptive Complexity
abstract_short: Textbook establishing the correspondence between logical definability and computational complexity. Shows least-fixpoint logic (and hence Datalog) captures PTIME on ordered structures.

title: Logic Programs with Stable Model Semantics as a Constraint Programming Paradigm
venue: Annals of Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence
abstract_short: Proposes logic programming with stable model semantics as a new constraint programming paradigm, founding Answer Set Programming as a declarative problem-solving approach.

title: Strictly Declarative Specification of Sophisticated Points-To Analyses
abstract_short: Presents Doop, a framework expressing Java points-to analyses entirely in Datalog. Achieves performance matching hand-coded analyzers through aggressive optimization of recursive programs.

title: Using Datalog with Binary Decision Diagrams for Program Analysis
abstract_short: Describes bddbddb, a system implementing Datalog using BDDs to efficiently represent large relations, enabling context-sensitive pointer analysis of large Java programs.

title: Survey of Graph Database Models
abstract_short: Comprehensive survey of graph database models covering data structures, query languages, and integrity constraints from early network models through modern property graphs and RDF.

title: Declarative Networking
abstract_short: Introduces Network Datalog (NDlog) for declarative network protocol specification and presents relaxed semi-naive evaluation for asynchronous distributed settings.

title: Provenance Semirings
abstract_short: Unifies provenance models for databases using semirings, showing that bag semantics, probabilistic databases, and why-provenance are instances of the same algebraic framework. Extends to Datalog.

title: Datalog+/-: A Family of Languages for Ontology Querying
abstract_short: Defines the Datalog+/- family extending Datalog with existential quantification and equality in rule heads while ensuring decidability, enabling ontological query answering over large datasets.

title: Differential Dataflow
abstract_short: Introduces differential computation extending incremental computation to support arbitrarily nested iteration. Maintains computation results efficiently as inputs change incrementally.

title: Naiad: A Timely Dataflow System
abstract_short: Presents the timely dataflow model and Naiad system combining high-throughput batch processing, low-latency stream processing, and iterative computation using logical timestamps for coordination.

title: Datalog and Recursive Query Processing
abstract_short: Comprehensive survey of Datalog covering classical foundations, modern implementations, and applications in program analysis, networking, security, and data integration.

title: Querying Graph Databases
abstract_short: Tutorial studying expressiveness and complexity of graph query languages including regular path queries, conjunctive regular path queries, and their extensions with inverses and data tests.

title: SociaLite: Datalog Extensions for Efficient Social Network Analysis
abstract_short: Extends Datalog with aggregation, choice, and recursive aggregate functions for efficient social network analysis, demonstrating orders-of-magnitude speedups on graph analytics.

title: Design and Implementation of the LogicBlox System
abstract_short: Describes LogicBlox, a commercial Datalog-based platform for enterprise software supporting LogiQL language with incremental maintenance, transactions, and data analytics.

title: The Gremlin Graph Traversal Machine and Language
abstract_short: Formalizes Gremlin as a graph traversal machine with automaton and functional properties supporting imperative/declarative querying, host language agnosticism, and distributed execution.

title: Souffle: On Synthesis of Program Analyzers
abstract_short: Presents Souffle, a Datalog engine synthesizing native parallel C++ analyzers from logic specifications, enabling points-to analysis on OpenJDK7 in under a minute.

title: On Fast Large-Scale Program Analysis in Datalog
abstract_short: Introduces program synthesis methodology for Datalog specifications producing monolithic C++ analyzers with specialized data structures and parallel evaluation strategies.

title: QL: Object-Oriented Queries on Relational Data
abstract_short: Describes QL (later CodeQL), an object-oriented dialect of Datalog with classes and virtual dispatch that compiles to plain Datalog, used for semantic code analysis at scale.

title: Foundations of Modern Query Languages for Graph Databases
abstract_short: Comprehensive survey of graph query language foundations covering edge-labelled and property graph models, graph patterns, navigational expressions, regular path queries, and CRPQs.

title: Cypher: An Evolving Query Language for Property Graphs
abstract_short: Describes the Cypher property graph query language originally designed for Neo4j, covering its MATCH/RETURN pattern matching paradigm, formal semantics, and evolution toward standardization.

title: G-CORE: A Core for Future Graph Query Languages
abstract_short: Proposes G-CORE as a composable graph query language core with paths as first-class citizens, balancing path query expressivity and evaluation complexity for future graph query languages.

title: The Vadalog System: Datalog-Based Reasoning for Knowledge Graphs
abstract_short: First implementation of Warded Datalog+/-, a PTIME-complete Datalog extension for ontological reasoning over knowledge graphs with aggressive termination control.

title: Graph Pattern Matching in GQL and SQL/PGQ
abstract_short: Describes the graph pattern matching core shared by GQL (ISO graph query language standard) and SQL/PGQ (SQL extension for property graphs), covering syntax, semantics, and design rationale.

title: Modern Datalog Engines
abstract_short: Survey of modern Datalog engine architectures covering compilation strategies, parallel evaluation, incremental maintenance, and applications in program analysis and data integration.

title: An Analysis of Magic Sets and Related Optimization Strategies for Logic Queries
abstract_short: Provides formal analysis of magic set transformation and related optimizations for logic queries, characterizing when and why these transformations improve query evaluation.

title: Querying Regular Graph Patterns
abstract_short: Studies regular graph patterns combining conjunctive queries and regular path queries, establishing complexity bounds and practical evaluation algorithms for graph databases.

title: Demystifying Graph Databases: Analysis and Taxonomy
abstract_short: Comprehensive taxonomy of graph database systems analyzing data organization, system designs, graph query languages, and comparing property graph and RDF-based approaches.

title: On the Declarative Semantics of Deductive Databases and Logic Programs
venue: Foundations of Deductive Databases and Logic Programming
abstract_short: Introduces perfect model semantics and local stratification for logic programs, generalizing stratified semantics to a broader class of programs with negation.

title: Complexity and Expressive Power of Logic Programming
abstract_short: Survey of computational complexity results for logic programming covering data complexity, expression complexity, and connections between logic program classes and complexity classes.
